result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as test code, at any depth and with backslash paths. The `codeanalyzer` suite passes (333 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped).

**Change** — `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: the two `Mock resources` regexes (`__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` and `mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`) are replaced by one:

```java
".*/(__)?mock[^/\\\\]*/.*"
```

The folder-name part is `[^/\\]*`, so the match stays inside one folder name and accepts any punctuation or non-ASCII characters. Paths like `remock/`, `demo/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not matched. `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match. The existing `mockapi`, `_mock.*` and `[Mm]ocks` conventions are untouched.

**New test** — `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`: checks the new positives (`mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/`, `mock模拟/`, backslash paths), the previously supported folders, and the negatives.

I did not add a `Mock` (capitalised) rule. The old rule was case-sensitive too, apart from the `[Mm]ocks` line, which I left alone.
